one_month_reasoning: No earnings in the window: Q2 came out Aug 10 and Q3 2025 was reported Nov 10, so Q3 2026 most likely lands around Nov 9-12, after Oct 31. Inside the window: the September production update (mid-October; the Aug update came Sep 17). It should show self-mining around 80+ EH/s and AI ARR near $86M, probably with little new. Other things that can move it: ATM sales under the new $1B program (an overhang), any news on the A201 contract or a Rockdale lease (upside tail), and BTC/hashprice moves, which drive miner stocks day to day. The stock fell from ~$12.3 to ~$10.5 over Sep 23-30. Short-term reversal and negative momentum roughly cancel out, so I center on spot (P(>=10.64)=0.495) with monthly sigma ~29%, close to 108%/3.5 = 31%, and take no directional view.

fair_value.method: Blend of a DCF ($7.94; blended WACC 12.5%, g 2.5%, with Tydal at 90% NOI and prob-weighted AI/Rockdale growth), an asset SOTP ($7.39), EV/MW ($11.04) and peer EV/NTM-sales ($20.1) at weights 0.35/0.25/0.25/0.15, giving $10.4. Cash-flow methods sit below spot because mining loses half its subsidy at the April 2028 halving and net debt is ~$1.37B. Market multiples sit above spot.

bear.story: BTC/hashprice falls back to the June lows (~$28/PH/day) or the halving gets priced in early. Mining burns cash, BIT loans need collateral top-ups, and the $1B ATM is sold below $10. Tydal slips past Dec-31 or the Volta credit backstop milestone falters. No new colocation tenant. Equity is squeezed by ~$2B of gross debt.

base.story: Tydal phases 1-2 are delivered roughly on time and start ~$230M/yr of 90%-margin NOI. A102 and A201 come online and AI ARR reaches ~$300-400M run-rate. Mining is decent at ~$35-40 hashprice ahead of the 2028 halving. Rockdale HPC talks continue but nothing large is signed. Moderate ATM dilution. Stock trades near the blended fair value of ~$10.4.

bull.story: A second large colocation lease (Rockdale 300+ MW or Norway phase 3/Molde) is signed at Tydal-like economics (~$12M net value per MW), and BTC goes back above $110k. The market re-rates BTDR toward the contracted-AI cohort's EV/sales. Consensus PT ~$22.

thesis_break_reason: Below $6 the stock would be under the 52-week low ($6.92) and well under the Feb-2026 registered direct price ($7.94). Equity would be only ~$1.6B against ~$2B of gross debt (converts, BIT loans, the 3,669 BTC loan). That most likely means a fundamental failure: a Tydal delay or a lost credit backstop, a funding squeeze forcing deeply dilutive equity, or a hashprice collapse making mining cash-negative. Ordinary BTC volatility would not explain it.

reasoning: Primary-document work. Q2 2026 6-K: revenue $228.8M, gross loss -$8.5M, adj. EBITDA $31.1M, 73 EH/s, cash $496M, total debt $1.8B, Q2 capex $266M, $457M raised by ATM. The 9/29 interim financials and Recent Developments add things the recaps skip: four converts with $1.215B face, the Feb-26 notes converting at ~$9.93 (in the money near spot), a $423M BIT asset-backed loan, a 3,669-BTC loan, a no-fee tenant termination right at year 10 of the Tydal lease, 90% NOI, ~$1.3B of LCs, and rig lives cut to 2-3 years. Monthly updates show 79.9 EH/s, AI ARR $86M, A102 fully contracted (>$800M) and a 206.5 MW AI pipeline. My DCF (blended WACC 12.5%, g 2.5%) gives ~$7.9 and the asset SOTP ~$7.4: mining cash flows shrink after the 2028 halving and debt is heavy. Peer EV/MW gives ~$11.0 and the CoinShares EV/NTM-sales cohort gives ~$20 (that sector is richly priced; consensus PT $21.79). The weighted fair value is ~$10.4, close to spot $10.64. Insiders (CFO, CSO) bought ~$0.45M near $9 in August, a mild positive. The ladder is a three-scenario lognormal mixture: bear $5 (30%, sigma 0.45), base $10.5 (45%, sigma 0.33), bull $21 (25%, sigma 0.35). That puts the median ~$9.8 and the mean ~$11.5, with a fat right tail from lease optionality and a fat left tail from leverage and halving risk. Overall spread is consistent with ~90-100% vol, a bit below the trailing 108%. Limits: Twelve Data stats/estimates and Alpha Vantage were unavailable (plan/rate limits). A press claim of a September $300M note offering could not be found in EDGAR (no such 6-K through 9/29), so I ignored it. I did not look at options data.
